newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market closed sharply lower on Thursday, erasing earlier gains after markets were depressed by the publication of a poll predicting a slim majority for French President Chirac in the coming election.
"People are afraid that France could change its pro-Europe stance," a dealer in Madrid said.
But technical reasons were also behind the fall.
"The market has risen a lot, so it was a good excuse to take profits," he added.
Also the peseta, trading at around 84.33/34 lost ground from its opening levels of around 84.25/27 per mark.

Investors, though pleased by the EU Commission report predicting Spain will be part of EMU from the start, said at the long end yields are likely to remain highly volatile. The shorter end looked more attractive.
"Soon people will focus once more on the prospect of another official rate cut. Especially at the short end of the yield curve, we will soon see big interest," a dealer said.
On Monday the Spanish Treasury will auction one-year bills and, for the first time, 18-month bills.
